description: This GeoNode is the spatial data platform of COPECO, the Honduran national agency for disaster risk management and contingencies. It holds about 1,250 layers, all loaded in 2025, that underpin risk maps for the country and its municipalities: flood extents for rivers such as the Ulúa at 25 and 50 year return periods, landslide susceptibility for individual municipalities, drought hazard, soils and temperature, together with exposure layers such as national, departmental, municipal and urban road networks, bridges and water tanks. Coverage is national, with detailed layers for the Sula valley and other northern municipalities. Each layer has a download link and OGC map and feature services, and the API lists them all, so the data are free and available to download; the licence is recorded as not specified. Caveats: layer names are terse codes with thin metadata, several layers are versions of the same theme, and the licence needs confirming before redistribution. Simulation uses: mapping the exposure of roads, bridges and shelters to floods and landslides, planning evacuation routes, and prioritising emergency response by municipality. Related records: the Copernicus EMS on-demand mapping (data-copernicus-ems-on-demand-mapping) covers past Honduran flood events, and Healthsites.io (data-healthsites-io) can add health facilities to the exposure picture.
